nodes.name: Co-precipitation synthesis of PBAs
nodes.procedure: The coprecipitation synthesis of PBAs generally consists of the dropwise addition of an MX salt solution (X = Cl-, NO3-, SO42-, etc.) to a solution of A6-x[M'^(x+)(CN)6]. The M ion coordinates to the [M'^(x+)(CN)6]^(6-x)- unit, while A ions can be incorporated into the structure.

nodes.name: Soft-templating CoHCFe synthesis
nodes.procedure: By using different surfactants in Co(NO3)2 solution, Liu et al. were able to prepare different morphologies of cobalt hexacyanoferrate (CoHCFe). The nature of the surfactant can direct how the particles will grow. Sodium dodecyl benzene sulfonate (SDBS) forms droplets covered by the cobalt salt, leading to CoHCFe-covered SDBS spheres. Sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) covers the particle surface, producing SDS-covered CoHCFe cubes.

nodes.name: Citrate-assisted CoHCFe nanoframe synthesis
nodes.procedure: Nai et al. prepared CoHCFe nanoframes in the presence of trisodium citrate. Initially, typical cubes of CoHCFe are formed. However, with increased reaction time, the inner part of the cubes is consumed and reprecipitated at the edges of the original cubes, producing porous frames after 36 h of reaction. The citrate plays a key role as it protects the (100) faces of the cubes, leaving exposed reactive (110) edges.

nodes.name: PBA etching
nodes.procedure: Etching of PBAs using HCl, NH4OH, or NaOH to achieve porosity and hollowness. The etchant acts on the most reactive or weakest part, normally the corners or edges, producing cages. Protective agents like CTAB or PVP can direct the etching process.

nodes.name: Thermal oxidation to metal oxides
nodes.procedure: Thermal treatment in air, synthetic air, or oxygen at temperatures from 250°C to 900°C to convert PBAs to metal oxides. For example, calcination of hollow PB particles at 250°C or 400°C produces different phases of Fe2O3 depending on particle size.

nodes.name: Phosphorization to metal phosphides
nodes.procedure: Thermal treatment with NaH2PO2 powder under inert gas flow (Ar or N2) at 300-500°C to convert PBAs to metal phosphides.
